name: MAX4466 electret microphone amplifier
description: Electret microphone with a MAX4466 op-amp preamp and a gain trimmer (about 25x to 125x). OUT is the audio waveform, DC biased at VCC/2 and rail-to-rail, so silence reads a steady VCC/2 and loudness is the peak-to-peak swing. Runs on 2.4–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Electret Microphone Amplifier - MAX4466 with Adjustable Gain (product #1063, 3-pin header OUT, GND, VCC), also the generic GY-MAX4466 clone modules.
eli5: A tiny ear with its own amplifier. Its OUT pin sits at half the supply voltage when it's quiet and wiggles up and down with sound; the louder the sound, the bigger the wiggle.

pins.description: Audio output (pin 1): the microphone waveform, DC biased at VCC/2, swinging up to both supply rails. Connect to an ADC pin.

buildNotes: Header order as printed on the board: OUT, GND, VCC.
Power VCC from 3.3 V on an ESP32, Pico or Raspberry Pi: OUT is rail-to-rail, so a 5 V supply could put 5 V on the ADC pin.
OUT goes straight to an ADC pin: no capacitor or extra amplifier needed.
In silence OUT sits at VCC/2 (1.65 V on 3.3 V). Measure loudness as the peak-to-peak spread of fast samples over about 50 ms.
Set the gain with the small trimmer on the back: flat tops at 0 V or VCC mean the gain is too high.
On the ESP32 use an ADC1 pin (GPIO32–39); the Raspberry Pi has no ADC, so add one.

driver.code:
# MAX4466 electret microphone amplifier breakout (Adafruit #1063, header OUT, GND, VCC), MicroPython driver.
# The MAX4466 is a plain analog op-amp (Analog Devices/Maxim MAX4465-MAX4469 datasheet): no bus, no
# registers. The breakout biases its rail-to-rail output at VCC/2 and the audio rides on that level
# (DC coupled). Silence = a steady VCC/2; louder sound = a bigger swing around it, up to the supply rails.
# Gain is set by the trimmer on the back (about 25x to 125x).
# Loudness is therefore measured as the peak-to-peak spread of fast ADC samples over a short window
# (50 ms covers frequencies down to 20 Hz), exactly as Adafruit's own example does.
from machine import ADC, Pin
import time


class MAX4466:
    def __init__(self, out, vref=3.3):
        """out: GPIO number (or Pin) wired to OUT. vref: ADC full scale in volts, used when
        read_uv() is not available (e.g. Pico, where full scale is the 3.3 V supply)."""
        self.adc = ADC(Pin(out) if isinstance(out, int) else out)
        try:
            self.adc.atten(ADC.ATTN_11DB)  # ESP32: about 0-3.3 V input range; other ports have no atten()
        except AttributeError:
            pass
        self.vref = vref

    def voltage(self):
        """One OUT reading in volts."""
        if hasattr(self.adc, 'read_uv'):
            return self.adc.read_uv() / 1e6
        return self.adc.read_u16() * self.vref / 65535

    def bias(self, n=64):
        """Average OUT level in volts: the VCC/2 bias point (about 1.65 V on a 3.3 V supply)."""
        total = 0
        for _ in range(n):
            total += self.voltage()
        return total / n

    def peak_to_peak(self, window_ms=50):
        """Spread (max - min) of OUT over window_ms, in volts: the loudness figure.
        About 0 in silence; at most the supply voltage (the output is rail-to-rail)."""
        lo = hi = self.voltage()
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < window_ms:
            v = self.voltage()
            if v < lo:
                lo = v
            elif v > hi:
                hi = v
        return hi - lo

# MAX4466 electret microphone amplifier (MAX4466)

## Overview
The **MAX4466** (Analog Devices / Maxim) is a low-power op-amp made for microphone preamps. Hobbyists buy it on the **Adafruit Electret Microphone Amplifier - MAX4466 with Adjustable Gain (product #1063)**: an electret mic, the MAX4466 and a gain trimmer (about **25x to 125x**) on a small 3-pin board. Generic purple/blue "GY-MAX4466" clones copy the same design.
- **OUT** carries the audio waveform, **DC biased at VCC/2** (DC coupled). In silence it sits steady at VCC/2 (1.65 V on 3.3 V).
- The output is **rail-to-rail**: loud sound swings it from near 0 V to near VCC.
- It is an analog signal, not a sound-level (dB) meter. Measure loudness as the **peak-to-peak** swing over a short window.

## Pinout (Adafruit #1063 header, as printed on the board)
| Pin | Name | Function |
|-----|------|----------|
| 1 | OUT | Audio out, biased at VCC/2 |
| 2 | GND | Ground |
| 3 | VCC | Supply, 2.4–5.5 V |

## Electrical limits
- Supply: **2.4–5.5 V** (datasheet supply range; printed on the board as "VCC: 2.4-5.5V").
- Current: amplifier 24 µA typical (48 µA max), plus the electret mic bias (well under 1 mA).
- OUT swings to both supply rails. **On an ESP32, Pico or Raspberry Pi, power it from 3.3 V** so OUT never goes above 3.3 V. 3.3 V is also the "quietest" supply.

## Interface details
- Analog only: connect OUT straight to an ADC pin (no capacitor or extra amplifier needed).
- Silence = VCC/2. Loudness = max − min of fast samples over ~50 ms (covers down to 20 Hz).
- Turn the trimmer on the back to set the gain: too high and loud sounds clip at the rails, too low and quiet sounds barely move the ADC.

## Wiring
| Board | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) (pin 36) | 3.3 V (pin 1) |
| GND | GND | GND | GND (pin 6) |
| OUT | GPIO32–39 (ADC1) | GP26/27/28 (ADC) | External ADC (e.g. ADS1115/MCP3008) |

On the ESP32 use ADC1 pins (ADC2 stops working while Wi-Fi is on). The Raspberry Pi has no ADC.

## Using the driver
```python
from max4466 import MAX4466
import time
mic = MAX4466(34)          # GPIO wired to OUT
while True:
    print('bias=%.2fV p-p=%.2fV' % (mic.bias(), mic.peak_to_peak()))
    time.sleep(0.2)
```
`peak_to_peak(window_ms=50)` returns the swing in volts; `bias()` averages the DC level; `voltage()` is one reading (`read_uv()` on ESP32, else `read_u16()` × 3.3 V).

## Gotchas
- **5 V supply + 3.3 V board**: OUT can swing to 5 V and damage the GPIO. Use 3.3 V.
- **One reading means nothing**: the signal is a wave around VCC/2. Use peak-to-peak.
- **Noisy supply = noisy audio**: USB 5 V and Wi-Fi bursts show up on OUT. Use 3.3 V and keep wires short.
- **Clipping**: flat tops at 0 V / VCC mean the gain trimmer is too high.

## Datasheet
https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/MAX4465-MAX4469.pdf. Board: https://www.adafruit.com/product/1063
